Set up a GenAI prompt

Put a one-click AI command on any LN screen, check its answer, improve it, and take it away.

Status
Walked Oct 2026
Module
Tools, Warehousing
Length
7 tasks, 62 steps
Updated
22 Oct 2026
Applies to
Infor LN

Start

Summary

TaskWhat you doResultSteps
1Plan the promptThe session code, the table, the values and the sentence the user sees.6
2Model the datasetThe fields the answer needs are ready to send.15
3Write the promptA prompt exists with a label, a dataset and both texts.12
4Link the prompt to a sessionThe command is in the Actions menu of the screen.4

Before you start

  • An idea worth a prompt. Does the answer take more than one screen or record? Does somebody read it before acting on it? Is the work wording or a judgement on text, not a calculation? Can the screen's record reach the data? A no to any of them means a prompt does not help.
  • One record of each kind the prompt tells apart, to test the answer with.
  • GenAI switched on for your company's LN. Until someone with the Admin role switches on GenAI Embedded Experience in the CloudSuite Self-Service Portal, no AI command appears.

Procedure

1Plan the prompt

Result
The session code, the table, the values and the sentence the user sees.
Screen
Warehousing➔Inventory Reporting➔Inventory Position➔Company - Item Inventory (whwmd4100m100)

Why LN works this way. A prompt is tied to one exact session code, and its dataset to that session's table. From that table a dataset reaches the tables it points to and the tables that point at it, and nothing beyond. So the build starts with what the answer must say, and then finds the screen whose record owns that data. The example's stock rows belong to an item's warehousing record, which is what Company - Item Inventory lists. LN has no language model of its own: it keeps a list retrieved from the Infor GenAI application, and a prompt that names no model uses the one that service marks as default.

StepActionYou should see
1.1List the values the answer must state. Example: an item's stock in each warehouse, and each planned receipt and issueWrite downvalues
1.2Open a screen that lists the record those values belong to. Example: Company - Item InventoryOne row for each record. Example: an item on each row
1.3Read the code in the status bar at the foot of the screen. On a tab of a workbench, read it in the tab's own Personalization➔Personalize Form… insteadExample: whwmd4100m100Write downsession code
1.4Note the table the screen's records are in, or your best guess. A wrong guess is named by the first run. Example: whwmd400Write downtable
1.5Write the one sentence the user will see. Example: Check where this item's stock is and what is planned in and out.Write downinstruction text
1.6Open GenAI LLMs, Tools➔Application Extensibility➔Embedded GenAI➔GenAI LLMs and find the row with Is default ticked. That model answers a prompt that names noneOne model is the defaultWrite downmodel
Plan the prompt: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
The screen's table is not knownBuild the dataset on your best guess. A wrong table stops the first run with an error that names the right one
The screen you wanted cannot reach the dataPut the command on a screen whose record owns the data, as How far a dataset reaches sets out

2Model the dataset

Result
The fields the answer needs are ready to send.
Screen
Tools➔Application Extensibility➔Embedded GenAI➔Datasets (ttrpi5100m000)

Why LN works this way. A dataset is the LN data that travels with the question, and it is the whole of what the model is told. It starts from one main table and one index of it. The record the user is on reaches the dataset through that index, which is why both have to be the screen's own. Around the main table the Modeler offers two branches: Refers to, for a value behind a code, and Referred by, for rows that belong to the record. Every field ticked is sent, so take only what the prompt text will name.

StepActionYou should see
2.1Open Datasets and click NewDataset Configuration opens
2.2Enter a Dataset Name in lowercase and a Description. Example: item_stockWrite downdataset name
2.3Type your table in Main table. Example: whwmd400
2.4Set Selection Index to the screen's key. Example: 1 - Item
2.5Click OKThe Modeler lists the table's fields, none ticked
2.6Tick the fields of that index. Example: item
2.7Set the list above the Tables tree to By NameEach branch lists its tables in the order of their codes
2.8For a value behind a code, expand Refers to, choose the table and tick the field. Example: Items (tcibd001), then dsca and cuniThat table's fields. Example: Description and Inventory Unit
2.9For rows that belong to the record, expand Referred by
2.10Choose the table and tick its fields. Example: Item Inventory by Warehouse (whwmd215), then cwar, qhnd, qblk, qord and qallThat table's fields, none ticked until you tick them
2.11Do the same for each other set of rows. Example: Planned Inventory Transactions by Item (whinp100), then koor, orno, kotr, pono, qana, date and cwar
2.12For a name behind a code in those rows, expand the table and then its own Refers to. Example: under Item Inventory by Warehouse, Warehouses (whwmd200), then the Warehouses (tcmcs003) via Warehouse, and tick dscaThe path to the table, printed above the tree
2.13Read Selected Fields, under the two panels. If it is too short, drag the bar above it upward, but not to the top: the Modeler opens next time where you leave itSelected Fields lists every field ticked, under its table
2.14Click SaveNo message
2.15On Datasets, click RefreshYour dataset is listed
Model the dataset: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
It is not clear which index is the screen's keyOpen Find on the screen. Its first way to search is the key
A table cannot be found under Referred bySet the list above the tree to By Name, as in step 2.7, and go down to the table's code
The list under Referred by is too long to work downThe screen's table is too far from the data. Use a screen whose own table is one step from it
A field's code is not knownType part of its name in the box above Description
The Dataset Modeler shows no Tables or FieldsThe bar between the panels was left at the top, and the Modeler remembers it. Drag the thin bar under the toolbar down
The Dataset Modeler has no toolbar eitherThe bar is above the window. Make the window taller until the toolbar shows, then drag the bar down
The Tables tree goes blank after a searchThe search is still running. Clear the box above the tree and press Enter
The lookup on Main table lists nothingIt shows one package at a time. Type the table's code, as in step 2.3

3Write the prompt

Result
A prompt exists with a label, a dataset and both texts.
Screen
Tools➔Application Extensibility➔Embedded GenAI➔GenAI Prompts (ttrpi5150m000)

Why LN works this way. A prompt row ties a label, a dataset and two texts together. The label's description becomes the command's name. The instruction text is shown to the user beside the answer. The prompt text is what is sent to the model, with the dataset's output put where its data marker stands. The first prompt text is short on purpose: what the data is, the task, one rule and the marker.

StepActionYou should see
3.1Open GenAI Prompts and click NewA new row, holding another prompt's name and label
3.2Type your prompt's name over the one in GenAI Prompt. Example: stock_checkWrite downprompt name
3.3In the Label lookup, enter 2 under Language. 2 is English
3.4Enter a word under Label Description and press Enter. Example: InventoryLabels with that word
3.5Tick a label that reads as the command's name and click OK. Pick one no command on the screen uses. Example: Item InventoryThe label's name beside its code. Two labels can share a code, so check it is the one you tickedWrite downcommand name
3.6Type your dataset name in Dataset, over anything it holdsIts description shows beside it
3.7Set Usage Type, which sets the command's icon. Example: Report
3.8Click SaveA grey dot under each text column
3.9Tick the row, open the arrow beside Edit Text on the toolbar and choose InstructionNo text present; Create, Duplicate, Select or Exit?
3.10Choose Create, type your sentence and saveA last-modified stamp
3.11Close the editor, then open the arrow beside Edit Text, choose Prompt and CreateAn empty Text Editor
3.12Type the first prompt text, one line each, then save and close. Example: You are given an XML dataset for one item: its description and unit, its inventory in each warehouse, and its planned inventory transactions. Write a stock check for someone about to promise this item to a customer. Use only the information present in the dataset. #data,XML#A green tick under both text columns
Write the prompt: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
No text present when a text is openedNothing. The text has not been written yet; choose Create, as in step 3.10
The new row holds another prompt's valuesA new row is a copy of the row the cursor was on. Replace them, as in step 3.5 and step 3.6
The name beside the label is not the one tickedTwo labels share that code. Pick a label whose code has one name, as in step 3.5

4Link the prompt to a session

Result
The command is in the Actions menu of the screen.
Screen
Tools➔Application Extensibility➔Embedded GenAI➔GenAI Prompts by Session (ttadv9160m000)

Why LN works this way. Nothing shows on any screen until a prompt is linked to a session code. The link is to one exact code: the command appears on that session and on no other, however alike two screens look. Three settings on the link decide whether the command is offered, to whom, and with what selected.

StepActionYou should see
4.1Tick the prompt and choose References➔GenAI Prompts by Session. Do not open it from the menuThe prompt as the header, with no rows
4.2Click New and type your session code across the three Session boxes. Example: wh, wmd and 4100m100The screen's name appears, and Active is ticked. Example: Company - Item Inventory
4.3Set When Enabled. Always acts on the row in view or the ticked rows; Records Selected waits for a tick. Example: AlwaysFour values: Always, One Record Selected, Records Selected and Never
4.4Click SaveThe row stays
Link the prompt to a session: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
GenAI Prompts by Session opens with a session as its header, not the promptIt was opened from the menu, or with no prompt ticked. Step to your screen with the group arrows on the toolbar, click New and enter the prompt's name in GenAI Prompt; the link is the same
Enter a value for the Module field.The session is three boxes: package, module and code. Type the module in its own box, as in step 4.2

5Run it and check the answer

Result
A first answer, checked against the screen.
Screen
Warehousing➔Inventory Reporting➔Inventory Position➔Company - Item Inventory (whwmd4100m100)

Why LN works this way. When the command is chosen, LN runs the dataset for the record on the screen, writes the result into the prompt text and sends it to the model. The answer opens in a window of its own. The model answers only from what the dataset sent, and a wrong answer looks the same as a right one, so the first run is checked against the screen and then read for what nobody asked for.

StepActionYou should see
5.1Close any open tab of your screen
5.2Open your screen and tick a record whose answer you can check. Example: an item with stock in two warehouses
5.3Note the values the answer should state. Example: the item's on hand and on order figures on its rowWrite downexpected values
5.4Open Actions and choose your commandA window with your sentence under Prompt and the answer under Response
5.5Compare the answer with your expected valuesThe facts should match. Example: the warehouses' figures add up to the row's
5.6Read the answer for what the prompt text did not ask forExample: a report with a column of the model's own sums, one of them wrong, and a promise
Run it and check the answer: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
The command is not in ActionsRead the session code in the status bar of the screen and compare it with step 4.2, character for character. On a tab of a workbench the status bar shows the workbench; read the tab's code in its own Personalize Form, as in step 1.3
The command is still missing and the code is rightCheck that Active is ticked on the link, then close the screen's tab and open it again
The command is in Actions and greyedThe link waits for a ticked record. Tick one, or set When Enabled to Always, as in step 4.3
An error names dataset.get.selection.index and a tableThe dataset's main table is not the screen's. The table in the message is the screen's: build the dataset on it, or link the prompt to a screen on your table

6Improve it

Result
An answer in the form asked for, right for each kind of record.
Screen
Tools➔Application Extensibility➔Embedded GenAI➔GenAI Prompts (ttrpi5150m000)

Why LN works this way. A change to the prompt text is used by the very next run. A change to the dataset is not seen by a session that is already open. So a text change is tested where you stand, and a dataset change after the screen is opened again. Each line added here answers something the first answer got wrong or left out.

StepActionYou should see
6.1On GenAI Prompts, tick the prompt, open the arrow beside Edit Text and choose PromptThe text, in the editor
6.2Add a line above the marker that fixes the answer's form. Example: Output plain text only. No heading, no table, no list marks, no bold and no emoji.
6.3Add a line that forbids what the first answer added. Example: Do not calculate, total or subtract anything, and do not say what can be promised. Report the figures as they are.
6.4Add a line that says how the answer opens. Example: First line: the item, its description and its inventory unit.
6.5Add a line for one kind of row, with its values in order. Example: Then one line for each warehouse, written as: warehouse code and name: on hand, blocked, allocated, on order.
6.6Do the same for each other kind of row. Example: Then the planned inventory transactions, earliest transaction date first, one line each: date, warehouse, order type, order and line, transaction type, planned quantity.
6.7Add the exact words for when there is nothing to report. Example: If there are no planned inventory transactions, write "Nothing planned in or out."
6.8Add a line for the one thing the reader must not miss. Example: End with one sentence naming any warehouse with blocked stock, or saying there is none.
6.9Add a line for a missing value. Example: If a value you need is not in the dataset, write "[not available]" in its place.
6.10Add a line for how a date is written, then save and close. Example: Write every date as YYYY-MM-DD.A new last-modified stamp
6.11Choose your command again on the same record, without closing the screenThe answer in that form. Example: a line for each warehouse, then a line for each planned receipt and issue
6.12Compare it with your expected values againThe facts should match
6.13Choose your command on a record of each other kind. Example: an item with no stock that customers have ordered, and an item with nothingEach answer fits its record. Example: the two sales orders waiting; the words for nothing planned
6.14Optional: tick a field the answer still lacks in the Modeler, and save
6.15Optional: close the screen's tab and open the record againThe new field is in the answer
Improve it: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
The answer holds figures LN does notThe line against calculating is missing, step 6.3
The answer is a report or a letter againThe form line is missing, step 6.2
A value reads [not available]The record holds nothing there, the field is not ticked in the dataset, or the screen was open before the dataset was saved. Close its tab and open the record again, as in step 6.15
A type or a status prints as its code, such as act.slsAdd a line that names each code, as in A template for the two texts
The closing sentence names something that does not qualifyCheck it against the screen like any other line. The model can get a comparison wrong
The response contradicts the screenThe model reads only the dataset. Read Selected Fields, as in step 2.13, then open the screen again

7Remove it

Result
The command, the prompt and the dataset are gone.
Screen
Tools➔Application Extensibility➔Embedded GenAI➔GenAI Prompts (ttrpi5150m000)

Why LN works this way. LN will not delete a dataset while a prompt uses it, and deleting a prompt takes its links with it. So the prompt goes first and the dataset second, and the link needs no step of its own.

StepActionYou should see
7.1On GenAI Prompts, tick the prompt and click DeleteDelete the 1 selected record(s) ?
7.2Choose Yes1 records deleted
7.3On Datasets, tick the dataset, click Delete and choose Yes1 records deleted
7.4Close the screen's tab, open the screen again and open ActionsThe command is gone
Remove it: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
Unable to delete; record being used in other tableA prompt still uses the dataset. Delete the prompt first, as in step 7.1

Reference

  • A prompt is one click that reads and never writes. The user chooses the command, LN sends the record with the data its dataset names, and the answer opens in a window to read, copy or download. There is nowhere to type a question, and nothing is written back to LN.

    • Is the answer already on one screen?

      A good sign
      No. It takes several screens, or several records

      Seen here
      The example puts an item's stock in each warehouse and every planned receipt and issue in one answer

    • Does somebody read it before acting on it?

      A good sign
      Yes. A wrong answer reads like a right one

      Seen here
      Every answer carries LN's notice to verify it

    • Is the work wording, or a judgement on text?

      A good sign
      Yes, and not a calculation

      Seen here
      Left free, the model added sums of its own and one of them was wrong

    • Can the screen's record reach the data?

      A good sign
      Yes. How far a dataset reaches says how to tell

      Seen here
      The example was first wanted on the sales order line, which cannot reach an item's stock

    An idea that only restates one field saves nothing. A delivery update built here on one order line gave back three values of that line's own screen.

    The stock check fails the third question, so it is kept only as a demonstration. Its work is laying out figures LN already holds, and the rule against calculating leaves the model nothing to judge. LN shows the same data on screens of its own, Inventory 360 (whwmd4300m000), Warehousing➔Inventory 360, and Planned Inventory Transactions - Graphical View (whinp1300m000), Warehousing➔Inventory Planning & Analysis➔Planning➔Planned Inventory Transactions - Graphical View. The question a seller has, whether a quantity can be promised by a date, is available to promise, which LN checks itself. On the default model its answers changed from run to run, it could not be made to sort, and a long item comes back as a long block of text a sortable list shows better. Status Overview fits better: it reads a line's statuses and names the step that comes next.

  • Every prompt is these six decisions, and the example is one set of answers to them. Plan the prompt settles the first three and the last, and step 4.3 the fourth.

    • The screen

      How it is settled
      Go where the record that owns the data is listed, not where the user happens to be. A link is to one exact session code, read in the status bar, or on a tab of a workbench in the tab's own Personalize Form

      In the example
      whwmd4100m100, Company - Item Inventory

    • The table and its key

      How it is settled
      The dataset's main table has to be that screen's table, and its selection index the key the screen is viewed by

      In the example
      whwmd400, by 1 - Item

    • The fields

      How it is settled
      Only what the prompt text will name. Everything ticked is sent, and the model knows nothing else

      In the example
      The item with its description and unit, its stock in each warehouse, and its planned receipts and issues

    • One record or several

      How it is settled
      Always runs on the row the cursor is on, or on the ticked rows. Records Selected waits for a tick

      In the example
      Always

    • What is decided before the model is asked

      How it is settled
      A condition that must always hold is a row of the table's filter and not a sentence in the prompt

      In the example
      None

    • The sentence the user sees

      How it is settled
      The instruction text, shown beside the answer. It says what the command does

      In the example
      Check where this item's stock is and what is planned in and out.

  • A dataset starts at the screen's table and reaches in two directions only.

    • A table it points to, under Refers to

      What it adds
      One value on the record, a name behind a code. It opens to the tables it points to in turn

      In the example
      The item's description and unit

    • A table that points at it, under Referred by

      What it adds
      Rows that belong to the record. It opens to both branches of its own

      In the example
      A row for each warehouse, and a row for each planned receipt and issue

    • A table that points at a table it points to

      What it adds
      Nothing. Refers to never turns back

      In the example
      A sales order line reaches its item, and not the item's stock

    So the screen is chosen by where the data is. Three screens were weighed for the example.

    • Sales Order Lines

      Its record
      An order line

      Steps to the stock rows
      None. The line holds no stock figure and reaches its item only by Refers to

    • Inventory 360

      Its record
      An item

      Steps to the stock rows
      Two, through a list of tables too long to work down

    • Company - Item Inventory

      Its record
      An item's warehousing record

      Steps to the stock rows
      One

    To learn which table a screen is on, link a prompt to it and run it. A run on the wrong table is refused, and the message names the screen's table.

  • The instruction text is for the user and the prompt text is for the model. The answer window prints the instruction text in a box headed Prompt, and the prompt text is what is sent with the data.

    Infor's help defines the two texts and says nothing about how to write them. What follows is what the walked prompt texts hold and what their runs showed, a line of the prompt text at a time in the order the lines are typed.

    • What the data is

      What it is for
      Tells the model what the XML holds and how many records to expect

      Seen without it
      Not tried. The prompt texts read here open with it

    • The task

      What it is for
      What to write, and for whom

      Seen without it
      Not tried

    • Use only the dataset

      What it is for
      Keeps the model to the values it was sent

      Seen without it
      With this rule alone the figures LN sent were right, and the model still added sums of its own and said what could be promised

    • The form of the answer

      What it is for
      Plain text, one set line for each record, or a list

      Seen without it
      A report with headings and a table, its formatting marks showing. On another prompt, a letter with a greeting and a sign-off

    • No calculating

      What it is for
      Stops the model adding figures LN did not send

      Seen without it
      A column of the model's own subtractions, one of them wrong, and totals nobody asked for

    • A line for each part

      What it is for
      What to print, and in what order

      Seen without it
      The model chose the parts, and left the planned receipts and issues out

    • Every part, even when empty

      What it is for
      Keeps a part the model would drop

      Seen without it
      On a prompt about an order line, the list of its activities was left out until this was said

    • Which rows to print

      What it is for
      A filter the model applies to the rows it is sent

      Seen without it
      The same prompt printed every activity of the line, most of them not applicable. Told only to name the first activity not executed, it named one that did not apply

    • A name for a code

      What it is for
      The name behind a code the dataset cannot reach

      Seen without it
      The next step came back as a session code

    • Nothing to report

      What it is for
      The exact words for when no row qualifies

      Seen without it
      Not tried. Given the words, the model used them for a record with no rows and, on another prompt, for a dataset that arrived empty

    • The thing not to miss

      What it is for
      One closing sentence on what the reader must see

      Seen without it
      Not tried. Asked to compare allocated with on hand, it was wrong on three runs of four on an item with stock. Asked only which warehouses hold blocked stock, it named both, with their figures, and said there was none on two items without

    • A case of its own

      What it is for
      The words for a kind of record the general rule misreads

      Seen without it
      A canceled order line was given a next step

    • A missing value

      What it is for
      What to write for a value the dataset did not send

      Seen without it
      Not tried. With it, a blank description read [not available]

    • How a value is written

      What it is for
      One way of writing a date

      Seen without it
      Full timestamps on some runs of another prompt

    • The marker

      What it is for
      Where LN puts the data, as the last line

      Seen without it
      Not tried. The help says the data is then added to the end of the prompt

    Each line after the third was added because of an answer. The form line followed a report nobody asked for. The line against calculating followed a wrong sum. The lines for each part put back what the model had left out.

    A line that makes the model list what it received is a check on the dataset. One prompt here ends its answer with the code of every record in the dataset, and that line is how a ticked record that never reached the model was noticed.

    The marker is #data,XML#. XML was the only output format registered where these steps were written.

  • Square brackets mark what to replace. A line with none is typed as it stands, and the line for a kind of row is typed once for each kind.

    Instruction

    [What the command does, in one sentence.]

    Prompt

    You are given an XML dataset for [what one record is, and what comes with it].

    [What to write, and for whom].

    Use only the information present in the dataset.

    Output plain text only. No heading, no table, no list marks, no bold and no emoji.

    Do not calculate, total or subtract anything. Report the figures as they are.

    Write these parts in this order, and write every part, even when it is empty.

    First line: [what opens the answer].

    Then one line for each [kind of row], written as: [the values, in order].

    If there are no [rows of that kind], write "[the exact words]".

    For these codes, write the name instead of the code: [code] is [name]. Write any other code as it is.

    End with one sentence [on the one thing the reader must not miss].

    If a value you need is not in the dataset, write "[not available]" in its place.

    Write every date as YYYY-MM-DD.

    #data,XML#

    Start with the first three lines of the prompt text and the marker, and add the rest after an answer calls for them. That is the order of Write the prompt and Improve it, and it shows what each line changes.

    Name a field by the words of its description. The dataset sends qhnd under Inventory on Hand, and the example's text says on hand.

    The line for codes holds when a code outside its list arrives. Status Overview's text names four activity codes and says to write any other as it is. Later, two order lines carried a fifth activity, and the answer wrote it as its code.

  • The steps build one kind, a record with the rows that belong to it. The others differ in a choice of Plan the prompt, and each row says which.

    • One record, with the rows that belong to it

      What differs
      A table under Referred by for each set of rows, as in step 2.9

      Seen here
      The example: an item, its stock in each warehouse and its planned receipts and issues. A status check on a sales order line, with its blocking records, its activities and its deliveries

    • One record, as a message

      What differs
      The task names who the message is for, and Usage Type is Email

      Seen here
      A delivery update for a customer about one sales order line

    • Several ticked records

      What differs
      The link is to a screen that lists records, When Enabled stays Records Selected at step 4.3, and the task says what to do across the records

      Seen here
      A prompt on Business Partners that looks for one company entered twice. Of seven partners ticked, its answer listed six as received

    • One record each, several ticked

      What differs
      Nothing. A text written for one record answers for each ticked record in turn, in the list's order

      Seen here
      Status Overview and Shipments on four ticked sales order lines, each line answered in turn

    • A condition the data must meet

      What differs
      The condition is a row of the table's filter in the Modeler, by the Filter Present link on the Properties panel, and the prompt text only sets the answer out

      Seen here
      A prompt that lists sales orders by three conditions its dataset's filter applies. On another filtered dataset a ticked record did not reach the model, and no message said so

    • One dataset for several prompts

      What differs
      A filter row with Input ticked becomes a parameter of each prompt that uses the dataset, and its value is set on the prompt

      Seen here
      One prompt here has such a parameter, with a constant for its value. Not documented for this release.

    These steps build no filter. The filters described here were found in datasets that already existed.
